title: Sessions, Messages, And Streaming
objective: Wrap OpenCode and remote OpenWork session behavior behind workspace-first Server V2 routes and move the session UI onto those routes, including typed streaming helpers.

steps.name: Create the OpenCode session adapter layer
steps.description: Add a typed adapter over the OpenCode SDK or HTTP client that Server V2 can use for local workspace session operations without leaking OpenCode route shapes into handlers.
successFactors: Local session operations go through one adapter layer.
OpenCode-specific transport details stay server-internal.
The adapter is reusable across list, detail, message, and mutation routes.

steps.name: Create the remote OpenWork session adapter layer
steps.description: Add the client or proxy layer Server V2 will use when a workspace is backed by a remote OpenWork server so the same workspace-first API can route to remote backends.
successFactors: Remote session operations do not require direct client knowledge of remote backends.
The adapter can normalize remote responses into local server shapes.
Backend routing stays behind the server boundary.

steps.name: Implement session backend routing service
steps.description: Use workspace resolution to choose the local OpenCode adapter or the remote OpenWork adapter for each session operation so route handlers stay backend-agnostic.
successFactors: One service chooses the correct backend for a workspace.
The routing logic is reusable across all session endpoints.
Errors for unsupported or misconfigured backends are explicit.

steps.name: Implement `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/sessions`
steps.description: Add the workspace-first session list route that returns sessions for either local or remote workspaces through one normalized API shape.
successFactors: Session listing is workspace-first, not OpenCode session-first.
Local and remote workspaces both work through the same public route.
The response shape is typed and stable.

steps.name: Implement session detail routes
steps.description: Add routes for reading one session, its status, and its todo or summary surfaces in the workspace-first model.
successFactors: Session detail and status routes exist in the normalized namespace.
The payloads hide raw OpenCode transport details.
The routes are ready for app detail views and status chips.

steps.name: Implement session creation
steps.description: Add the route and service logic for creating a session inside a workspace, including the mapping to the correct local or remote backend primitive.
successFactors: Session creation is addressed by workspace ID first.
The server stores or resolves the backend mapping correctly.
The route is ready for optimistic app session creation flows.

steps.name: Implement session update and delete
steps.description: Add workspace-first session mutation routes for update and deletion so the UI can stop depending on legacy session transport paths.
successFactors: Session mutation routes are typed and normalized.
Local and remote backend calls map correctly.
Errors use the shared error and request-ID conventions.

steps.name: Implement message list and detail routes
steps.description: Add routes for listing and reading messages for a session under the workspace-first hierarchy.
successFactors: Message routes nest under workspace and session IDs.
The server returns normalized message data regardless of backend.
The route contract is documented in OpenAPI.

steps.name: Implement message send routes
steps.description: Add the primary message-send route for prompts or user input so the session composer can move onto Server V2.
successFactors: The route supports the message-send shape the app needs.
The server can forward to local OpenCode or remote OpenWork correctly.
Response handling works with optimistic UI flows.

steps.name: Implement message update and delete routes
steps.description: Add routes for deleting messages or message parts and updating message parts where the upstream backend supports it, while keeping the public API workspace-first.
successFactors: The server exposes message mutation primitives intentionally.
Unsupported backend cases are handled predictably.
The contract does not leak upstream path design.

steps.name: Implement advanced session control routes
steps.description: Add workspace-first routes for init, fork, abort, share, unshare, summarize, and any other required session control primitives called out in `ideal-flow.md`.
successFactors: The main advanced session controls are covered in the public API.
The server maps each control action to the correct backend call.
Route names stay consistent with the workspace-first model.

steps.name: Implement prompt_async, command, and shell routes
steps.description: Expose the execution-style session primitives needed by the app while keeping transport and policy inside the server.
successFactors: The server can express async prompt, command, and shell actions through one normalized API family.
These routes remain workspace-first and typed.
The app no longer needs to reach directly toward raw OpenCode session endpoints for them.

steps.name: Implement revert and unrevert routes
steps.description: Add the session history control routes used by undo or restore flows so the server owns these primitives instead of app-side transport code.
successFactors: Undo-style flows have a typed server route.
The app does not need special transport cases for revert operations.
Response shapes are consistent with other session mutations.

steps.name: Define the SSE contract
steps.description: Pick the one or two session-related SSE endpoints, define typed event payloads, and add them to the public contract instead of treating streaming as an undocumented side channel.
successFactors: The chosen SSE route(s) are documented in OpenAPI or companion contract metadata.
Event payload types are generated or shared from contract output.
The design matches the limited-SSE guidance in the planning docs.

steps.name: Implement server SSE endpoints
steps.description: Add the actual SSE streaming route(s) in Server V2 so the app consumes streaming only through the OpenWork server, not directly from OpenCode.
successFactors: The server exposes the chosen SSE route(s) end to end.
The server can proxy, normalize, or adapt backend stream events as needed.
Streaming failures are handled cleanly and visibly.

steps.name: Implement handwritten SDK stream helpers
steps.description: Add the small typed streaming helper(s) in `packages/openwork-server-sdk/src/streams/**` so SSE usage still feels like part of the same SDK surface.
successFactors: The SDK exports ergonomic typed stream helpers.
Event payload typing comes from generated or shared contract types.
The app can call streaming through `createSdk({ serverId })`.

steps.name: Migrate session list and detail UI
steps.description: Move session list, session detail, and message history reads onto Server V2 through the adapter so the UI consumes the normalized routes for its main read surfaces.
successFactors: The session UI uses Server V2 for the migrated reads when the flag is on.
Legacy fallback remains isolated.
The UI no longer needs raw OpenCode session path knowledge for those surfaces.

steps.name: Migrate composer send and session mutation flows
steps.description: Move the composer, prompt send, session creation, and core session mutation paths onto the new routes so the UI is no longer split across old session transports.
successFactors: The app can send prompts and create sessions through Server V2.
Optimistic UI behavior still works with the new transport.
Temporary normalization or fallback logic is limited to the migration boundary.

steps.name: Add session integration tests
steps.description: Write integration coverage for local OpenCode-backed sessions, remote-server-backed sessions, advanced control routes, and error cases so the main product surface is not validated only manually.
successFactors: The core session route family is covered by automated tests.
Local and remote backend behaviors are both exercised.
Common failure shapes are asserted.

steps.name: Add streaming verification
steps.description: Add tests or deterministic verification for SSE subscription, typed event handling, reconnect or end-of-stream behavior, and app consumption through the SDK helper.
successFactors: Streaming works from server to SDK helper to app code.
Typed event shapes are validated.
The app does not connect directly to underlying OpenCode SSE routes.
